title: Chris Kelly's band and his wah-wah cornet
summary: Chris Kelly played parties for all kinds of audiences; his speciality was Careless Love with the wah-wah mute.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Well anyhow, let's see, you played with that band on drums.
Yeah, and different bands with Chris, different parties. Chris used to play mostly parties on the weekdays, you know.
Who did he play for, Chris?

Well he played like the rest of the bands. He was a named band and he was good, his style of playing. He played for a lot of Italian people, Italian halls, but mostly for colored. See he wasn't particular about the way he played, as long as he was playing.
Did he play for rich people, all kinds?
All kinds, all sorts of people.
He did. What style of music did he feature, Chris?
Well you mean like the songs? Well his special song was Callous Love. That's where the wah-wah came in at. He really could do the wah-wah on the cornet. He didn't play a trumpet, he played cornet.
Was there any special reason for playing cornet?
No, I didn't know. I wouldn't know about that, why he played it, but that's what he played, the cornet.
